quizzes.title: India's position in the CPI 2025
quizzes.passage: The Corruption Perceptions Index is released by Transparency International, a non-profit organisation whose aim is to combat global corruption through civil society anti-corruption measures. The index assesses public sector corruption and is described as a leading global indicator of that problem. The 2025 edition applies the same measure to every country covered, so that results can be compared across countries. It highlights global trends and structural causes, and it recommends measures to strengthen institutional integrity. The latest edition reports that the global average score has declined to its lowest level in over a decade, which indicates worsening corruption trends worldwide. Only a small number of countries now score above 80, compared with a larger number a decade ago. Many countries still fall in the serious-concern range, with most nations scoring below 50. India's position in the latest edition is of particular interest to readers in the country. Its performance is assessed against the global average, and the booklet compares it with several South Asian neighbours. The comparison shows that India performs better than some countries in its region, while it lags behind others. The booklet concludes that these results point to scope for institutional strengthening.

questions.q: What is the global average CPI score in 2025?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the global average CPI score as 42, the lowest level in over a decade.

questions.q: On the CPI scale, what does a score of 0 signify?
questions.explanation: The CPI scale runs from 0, meaning highly corrupt, to 100, meaning very clean.

questions.q: How many countries were assessed in CPI 2025?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the index covers 182 countries.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India performs better than China in the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025.
Reason (R): The booklet states that India lags behind China in the index.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says India lags behind China, so A is false while R is true.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India in CPI 2025:
I. India performs better than Sri Lanka.
II. India lags behind Bhutan.
III. India's score is above the global average.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is false because India's score is below the global average.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about India in CPI 2025 are correct?
I. India's score is 39 out of 100.
II. India lags behind China.
III. India was ranked 96th in CPI 2025.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III wrongly gives India's 2024 rank as its 2025 rank.

questions.q: Which of the following countries does India perform better than in CPI 2025?
questions.explanation: The booklet says India performs better than Bangladesh, while Bhutan and China rank above India.

quizzes.title: Bodies and instruments against corruption
quizzes.passage: Several international bodies and instruments deal with corruption, and the booklet describes some of the most significant ones. The United Nations Convention against Corruption, dated 2003, is an instrument that addresses corruption across the world. Within the G20, an anti-corruption working group, dating from 2010, is one of the bodies the booklet lists. The Financial Action Task Force, which acts as a global watchdog on money laundering and terrorist financing, is a body whose membership includes 38 countries and two organisations, among them the Gulf Cooperation Council and the European Union. The task force maintains lists of countries whose cooperation with it is considered weak, and these include a grey list with 21 countries and a second list with a different label. The Sustainable Development Goals also include a goal titled Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions. The booklet presents these bodies together, covering an international convention, a working group, a financial watchdog and a development framework, as part of the wider effort against corruption. Each entry in the booklet's summary gives a short description of the body or instrument concerned.

questions.q: Which country officially became a full member of the Financial Action Task Force, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says Indonesia officially became a full member of the FATF.

questions.q: Which of these countries is labelled on the FATF Black List as a Non-Cooperative Country or Territory?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Iran, North Korea and Myanmar as the countries on the Black List.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group, according to the booklet?
options: Set binding targets for national budgets
Investigate cross-border crime in real time
Maintain a list of non-cooperative territories
Share effective strategies to combat corruption, especially through emerging technologies
questions.explanation: The booklet says the G20 working group shares effective strategies to combat corruption, especially through emerging technologies.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The UN Convention against Corruption 2003 is the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument.
Reason (R): India ratified this convention in 2011.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but India's ratification in 2011 does not explain why the convention is the only binding universal instrument.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about international anti-corruption bodies:
I. The FATF was established in 1989 by the G7.
II. The G20 Anti-Corruption Working Group dates from 1989.
III. Indonesia officially became a full member of the FATF.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is false because the G20 working group dates from 2010.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. India ratified the UN Convention against Corruption in 2011.
II. The Sustainable Development Goal titled Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions is SDG 16.
III. Indonesia is listed on the FATF Black List.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is false because the Black List names Iran, North Korea and Myanmar.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Financial Action Task Force   ->   A. Established by the G7
II. FATF Black List   ->   B. Non-cooperative countries or territories
III. Sustainable Development Goal titled Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions   ->   C. Anti-corruption as an institutional principle
IV. UN Convention against Corruption   ->   D. Only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument
questions.explanation: The booklet links each body or instrument to exactly one of the descriptions in List II.
